chunks: Saad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Munhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Ziyad ibn Suqah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

He said: 'It is not objectionable for any one of you to pray in a single garment with its buttons unfastened, for the religion of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) is upright (straightforward/easy).'

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ الْوَاحِدِ: The single garment (referring to the upper wrap)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray with the top button of the garment unfastened?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the concept of 'Hanif' is interpreted not merely as monotheistic purity but as a principle of ritual ease and lack of excessive burden, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the flexibility of Sharia. This view is particularly significant in fiqh discussions regarding the minimum requirements for covering the awrah during prayer, allowing for practicality in daily worship. It underscores the Prophetic tradition of simplicity, contrasting with rigid formalism that might complicate the act of prayer.
